checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: 10,000 clients contend for one distributed lock. Which ZooKeeper recipe avoids a herd when the lock holder leaves?

options.label: Everyone watches the holder or parent
options.sub: all contenders retry after the shared watch fires
options.verdict: A holder or parent change wakes every contender. Thousands of clients then re-read the queue and race together, creating a thundering herd against the ensemble.

options.label: Watch the immediate predecessor
options.verdict: Sequence numbers establish a total queue order, while each contender watches only the node immediately before it. When the holder leaves, exactly one waiter is notified and advances.

defend.prompt: Defend the predecessor-watch recipe. Which statements are true?

options.label: Sequence numbers establish the contenders' queue order
Ephemeral nodes clean up after their owning sessions expire
A departing holder notifies only its immediate successor
Watches persist forever after they fire

defend.explain: ZooKeeper watches are one-shot, not permanent subscriptions. After a notification, the waiter must re-read the relevant state and reinstall the watch if it still needs one. The safe loop also handles the race where the predecessor disappears between the read and watch installation. Ephemeral sequential nodes preserve queue order, session expiry removes abandoned claims, and predecessor watches wake one waiter instead of all 10,000 contenders.

checkpoints.title: Quorum ladder
checkpoints.prompt: Reason about quorum and client sessions in a five-server ZooKeeper ensemble.

rungs.q: How many servers must persist a write before it commits?
rungs.note: A five-server ensemble needs a majority: floor(5 / 2) + 1 = 3 servers.

rungs.q: How many simultaneous server failures can the ensemble tolerate while retaining a write quorum?
rungs.note: Two failures leave three available servers, which is still a majority. A third failure leaves only two and writes stop.

rungs.q: A client briefly disconnects but reconnects before its session timeout. What can happen?
choices: Its session can recover and its ephemeral nodes remain
Its ephemeral nodes disappear immediately on disconnect
It must create a new ensemble quorum
rungs.note: A connection loss is not immediate session expiry. Reconnecting to an ensemble server before the timeout can recover the session and preserve its ephemeral nodes.

checkpoints.explain: ZooKeeper commits writes through a majority, so five servers require three acknowledgments and tolerate two simultaneous server failures. Client failure detection is governed by the session timeout, not a momentary socket disconnect. A short timeout detects real failures faster but can expire healthy clients during transient network trouble; a longer timeout improves recovery odds but delays ephemeral-node cleanup and failover.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build the path for a waiting contender to become leader.
checkpoints.explain: Each contender creates an ephemeral sequential ZNode and sorts the children by sequence number. A contender leads immediately if its node is initially lowest; the shown path is the non-lowest branch, which watches only its immediate predecessor. A notification is a hint, so the waiter re-lists the children and re-checks its position before leading or installing another predecessor watch. Session expiration deletes the owner's ephemeral node and allows the queue to progress. Watching the parent creates a herd, a persistent claim survives owner failure, and polling adds avoidable load and failover delay.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: An application leader or lock holder's ZooKeeper session expires, and the ensemble saturates for 20 seconds. Which signal identifies the root cause?
checkpoints.explain: All contenders watched the application holder's ZNode. When the holder's session expires, ZooKeeper deletes that ephemeral node, wakes all 9,800 watchers, and causes them to re-list the contenders together. The resulting getChildren spike is the thundering-herd symptom; the shared watch set is the root cause. Use ephemeral sequential contender nodes, sort by sequence number, and have each waiter watch only its immediate predecessor. A deletion then wakes one successor, which re-lists state and reinstalls its one-shot predecessor watch when needed.

wrong.Client Requests: The 180k getChildren requests per second are the immediate load spike, but they are a symptom: all contenders woke and re-listed because they shared a watch on the holder ZNode.
wrong.Write Quorum: Three of five servers remain healthy, so the ensemble still has the majority required for writes. Quorum health does not explain the synchronized client burst.
wrong.Transaction Log: A steady 4 ms fsync p99 does not indicate transaction-log saturation. The sharp change comes from 9,800 contenders waking from the shared holder-ZNode watch.
